mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: The threat for severe weather is expected to increase by early afternoon, likely requiring a new severe thunderstorm watch

details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for severe weather is expected to increase by early afternoon, likely requiring a new severe thunderstorm watch

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Recent trends in base velocity data indicate a strengthening cold pool with the leading edge of thunderstorms near Marion, IN. That convection is located to the north of an outflow boundary stretching from northwest through southeast IN. However, prevailing west-southwest low-level winds (per KIND VWP) will likely support the eastward movement of the boundary with resultant air mass recovery expected across portions of western OH by early afternoon. As such, it appears likely that the above-mentioned storms will continue to spread southeast into the discussion area within the next hour or so. Damaging wind gusts will be the primary hazard with the most intense storms

details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for damaging winds is expected to continue across the watch area this morning. Additional storm development is possible along a composite outflow boundary from northeast Kentucky into western Virginia by early afternoon, possibly requiring an additional watch issuance

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A mature MCS with embedded bowing structure is ongoing as of 1510Z across portions of central and southern OH with a wind gust to 82 mph reported within the past hour at the Columbus John Glenn International Airport. While that portion of the MCS is currently the most intense, considerable downstream convection present from southeast OH into northwest WV leads to uncertainty in the longevity of the damaging wind threat given the convectively overturned air mass. Potentially greater air mass destabilization is expected by early afternoon farther southwest from northeast KY into western portions of WV and VA, in the vicinity of a composite outflow boundary. There, storm intensification on the western flank of the OH MCS appears possible, along with additional in situ development along the boundary. While the region will reside on the southern fringe of stronger vertical shear, the presence of moderate to strong instability with steepening low-level lapse rates will support damaging wind potential with the strongest storms

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...55-70 MPH
